title: Traffic & Routing
summary: How a request finds a healthy server. 5 building blocks drilled by recall: the signal that says reach for one, what it costs, how it breaks, which sibling rules it out, and what it is doing across the canonical problems.
keyTakeaways: Load Balancer — A single address in front of many interchangeable servers, spreading requests and routing around dead ones.
Reverse Proxy — A server-side intermediary that terminates the client connection and speaks to backends on its behalf, so cross-cutting work happens once at the edge.
API Gateway — The single front door for external callers: authenticates, applies quota, routes to the right service, and normalises the response.
Service Discovery — A registry that answers 'where is service X right now', so callers reach live instances without hardcoded addresses.
DNS & Anycast Routing — Steering users to a region or PoP before a connection is ever made, using DNS answers or a single IP announced from many locations.

questions.prompt: Load Balancer vs DNS & Anycast Routing vs Service Discovery — what decides between them?
points: DNS & Anycast Routing — DNS steers between REGIONS; an LB steers between servers. Different blast radius, different failover speed.
Service Discovery — Discovery lets the caller pick a backend itself, removing the middle hop — normal for internal service-to-service.
Load Balancer — A single address in front of many interchangeable servers, spreading requests and routing around dead ones.
questions.answer: DNS & Anycast Routing: DNS steers between REGIONS; an LB steers between servers. Different blast radius, different failover speed. Service Discovery: Discovery lets the caller pick a backend itself, removing the middle hop — normal for internal service-to-service.

questions.prompt: Load Balancer appears in 5 of the canonical design problems. Name as many as you can, and say what it is doing in each.
points: Design a Chat System — Spreads long-lived socket connections across the chat fleet, where the stateless assumption breaks — a connection pinned for hours is not a request you can rebalance.
Design a Ride-Sharing Service — Distributes driver and rider connections across the matching fleet, rebalancing only on reconnect since an open socket cannot be moved.
Design a Collaborative Document Editor — Distributes collaborator sockets across the edit fleet, with everyone on one document needing to reach the same session owner.
Design a Live Streaming Service — Spreads viewer connections at broadcast start, when a million clients arrive inside the same few seconds rather than arriving smoothly.

Design an Authentication & Session Service — Fronts a stateless auth tier, which is what lets any node validate any session — and the reason session state lives in a shared store rather than server memory.

questions.prompt: Service Discovery vs Load Balancer vs DNS & Anycast Routing — what decides between them?
points: Load Balancer — A load balancer centralises the same decision; discovery distributes it to callers. One hop vs. one library everywhere.
DNS & Anycast Routing — DNS is discovery with weak TTL semantics — fine for coarse-grained, wrong for second-by-second membership.
Service Discovery — A registry that answers 'where is service X right now', so callers reach live instances without hardcoded addresses.

questions.prompt: Service Discovery appears in 4 of the canonical design problems. Name as many as you can, and say what it is doing in each.
points: Design a Distributed Rate Limiter — Gateways have to agree on which node owns a client's counter, so ring membership is shared state rather than a local assumption.
Design a Distributed Cache — Tells clients which nodes are on the ring right now; a stale membership view means two clients hash the same key to different nodes.
Design a Distributed Message Queue — Lets producers and consumers find the current leader for a partition, which moves whenever an election happens.
Design a Distributed Key-Value Store — Propagates ring membership so every node agrees on who owns which key range — usually by gossip rather than a central registry.

questions.prompt: DNS & Anycast Routing vs Load Balancer vs CDN — what decides between them?
points: Load Balancer — Use DNS to pick the region, an LB to pick the server. They compose; they do not compete.
CDN — A CDN already does global steering as part of its product — usually the cheaper answer for static content.
DNS & Anycast Routing — Steering users to a region or PoP before a connection is ever made, using DNS answers or a single IP announced from many locations.
